title: Delhi High Court denies ANI injunction against OpenAI
summary: India's landmark AI copyright case turned on evidence: ANI's cited articles postdated model training, and the judge treated LLM training as transformative.
body:
## The ruling

The Delhi High Court on July 27 declined to grant Asian News International a preliminary injunction against OpenAI, in the highest-profile AI copyright case brought in India. Justice Amit Bansal's interim order rejects ANI's request to restrain OpenAI from using its journalism in training and in ChatGPT outputs.

The evidentiary problem was decisive. Several articles ANI submitted as examples of copied work were published after the relevant model's training data cutoff, meaning they could not have been ingested — an inconsistency that undercut the broader infringement claim. Beyond that, the court found no demonstrated economic harm, reasoning that a news agency and an AI developer are not competitors in the same market. It also applied familiar copyright limits: the facts reported in an article are not protectable, and reproducing subject matter or headline-level information does not amount to competing with the original.

On training itself, the judge treated the ingestion of text for model training as falling within Indian copyright law's exception for private and research use, and assessed the activity as transformative under a three-part fairness test.

## What remains open

The order is interim and leaves the harder questions for trial: whether retrieval-augmented outputs that surface current articles constitute communication to the public, and whether trained weights amount to a lasting store of the underlying works. Those issues, not training-set ingestion, are where news publishers' strongest arguments now sit.

## Why it matters

India is the largest single market for ChatGPT by users, and ANI v. OpenAI has been the reference case for how a major non-Western jurisdiction outside the EU would treat AI training. A ruling that reads training as transformative and research-adjacent removes near-term legal risk from OpenAI's largest growth market and gives every developer operating there a citable precedent. It also demonstrates how thin the evidentiary base for these claims can be: the case turned less on doctrine than on a plaintiff unable to show the specific works in the specific model.
title_zh: 德里高等法院驳回印度通讯社 ANI 对 OpenAI 的禁令申请
summary_zh: 印度标志性 AI 版权案输在举证：ANI 举出的文章晚于模型训练截止日，法官同时认定大模型训练具有转化性。
body_zh:
## 裁定结果

德里高等法院 7 月 27 日驳回印度亚洲国际新闻社（ANI）针对 OpenAI 的临时禁令申请，这是印度迄今关注度最高的 AI 版权案。法官 Amit Bansal 的中间裁定，拒绝了 ANI 要求禁止 OpenAI 将其新闻用于训练及 ChatGPT 输出的请求。

举证问题是决定性的。ANI 提交的多篇「被抄袭」范例发表时间晚于相关模型的训练数据截止日，也就是根本不可能被收录——这一自相矛盾削弱了整体侵权主张。法院还认定未能证明经济损害，理由是通讯社与 AI 开发商并不处在同一竞争市场。裁定同时套用了版权法的常规边界：报道中的事实本身不受保护，复述题材或标题层面的信息不构成与原作竞争。

对训练行为本身，法官认为把文本吃进模型训练可落入印度版权法关于私人使用与研究的例外，并在三要件公平性测试下将其评定为具有转化性。

## 仍未解决的部分

该裁定属中间性质，把更硬的问题留给了正式审理：以检索增强方式呈现时新文章是否构成向公众传播，以及训练后的权重是否等同于对原作的持久存储。新闻出版方目前最有力的论点正落在这两处，而不在训练集摄入。

## 为何重要

印度是 ChatGPT 用户规模最大的单一市场，ANI 诉 OpenAI 一案一直被视为观察欧盟之外重要非西方司法辖区如何看待 AI 训练的标尺。将训练读作转化性使用、并向研究例外靠拢的裁定，为 OpenAI 最大的增长市场卸下了近期法律风险，也给所有在印度经营的开发者留下了可引用的先例。这一案还暴露出此类诉讼的举证基础有多薄：胜负不在法理，而在原告拿不出「哪一部作品进了哪一个模型」。

sources.title: Delhi High Court hands OpenAI a win by rejecting major Indian news agency's copyright injunction
